item.title: Shoulder — Dry Cupping / Myofascial Decompression
clinicalUse: Use when assessment identifies a relevant impairment in Shoulder and the parent technique fits the patient's presentation.
Primary treatment target: glenohumeral/scapular pain, elevation, rotation and functional reach.
Retain the technique only if it produces a meaningful within-session improvement.
patientPosition: Supine, side-lying or sitting with the arm supported.
Begin near a comfortable resting position in irritable presentations.
therapistPosition: Stand beside the shoulder and keep the arm close to the joint line when applying manual force.
stabilization: Stabilize the scapula/thorax when the target is glenohumeral; allow scapular motion when that is the intended target.
contact: Use broad contact over proximal humerus, scapula or relevant soft tissue and protect sensitive anterior structures.
Place an appropriate cup only on intact soft tissue with conservative suction.
Avoid vulnerable neurovascular areas, open skin and regions where a cup cannot be controlled safely.
forceDirection: Use the lowest negative pressure that creates a tolerable effect; static or movement-assisted application may be used when appropriate.
dosage: A conservative application is about 3–10 minutes per region, shorter for first exposure or sensitive skin.
steps: 1. Record the exact comparable sign for Shoulder: glenohumeral/scapular pain, elevation, rotation and functional reach.
2. Screen regional red flags, contraindications and technique-specific precautions before touching the patient.
3. Position and stabilize the patient so the target is comfortable and the manual input can be localized.
4. Apply a low-force trial using the parent technique principles and the region-specific contact described above.
5. Monitor pain quality, symptom distribution, guarding and patient confidence throughout.
6. Re-test the original comparable sign immediately after the trial.
7. Keep the technique only when the response is useful, then transfer the gain into active movement, loading or self-management.
mistakes: Applying the technique because it is familiar rather than because the examination supports it.
Using more force when the response is unclear or worsening.
Failing to re-test the exact movement or function that justified the treatment.
safety: Respect dislocation history, fracture, postoperative restrictions, acute inflammatory states and neurological symptoms.
Temporary discoloration can occur; more bruising does not mean a better treatment.
Stop or modify if symptoms peripheralize, neurological status worsens, the response is disproportionate or the patient asks to stop.
item.visualCue: Shoulder assessment → correct regional setup → Dry Cupping / Myofascial Decompression → immediate comparable-sign re-test.

subTechniques.name: Pectoralis minor/major — Dry Cupping / Decompression
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, side-lying or sitting with the arm supported.
subTechniques.contact: Appropriately sized cup placed on intact soft tissue over Pectoralis minor/major with low suction.
subTechniques.direction: Use the lowest suction that creates a tolerable effect; static or movement-assisted application as appropriate.
subTechniques.dosage: Conservative application approximately 3–10 minutes, shorter for first exposure or sensitive skin.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
